nodes.body: Explicit `compose.include.concept` entries copy display/version from the ValueSet, which may omit both. Validating `code1` against `ShapeCode1Vs` therefore returns true without `Display 1` or version `1.0.0`, even though the later status lookup finds the concept. Resolve missing metadata before constructing the result and checking the display, preserving metadata supplied by the expansion. Filling only a null result display later is insufficient: the input display may already have been copied into it. Add coverage for this enumerated-include case, including an incorrect input display.

Agreed, and fixed in the next push (not yet pushed when written): the code system is now resolved before the result is built, so an enumerated concept gets its display and version from the code system and the display check compares against that. Covered by `EnumeratedConceptGetsDisplayAndVersionFromCodeSystem`.

When the CodeSystem resolves, its metadata is not copied into the failure result. For example, `CodeInCodeSystemButNotInValueSet` finds `code2` in version `1.0.0`, but returns neither that version nor `Display 2`. Populate the resolved version and, when the concept exists, its display; #3631 requires these outputs even when `result` is false. Add assertions for both fields to that test.

Agreed, and fixed in the next push (not yet pushed when written): when the code system resolves, a false result now carries its version and, if the concept exists, its display. `CodeInCodeSystemButNotInValueSet` asserts both.

This status lookup ignores `component.Version`. If a pre-expanded ValueSet references version 1 but the resolver's unversioned default is version 2, a concept active in version 1 and retired in version 2 receives an incorrect retirement warning and inactive status while the response reports version 1. Resolve the version-qualified canonical when the expansion supplies a version, and add a regression test with different statuses across versions.

Agreed, and fixed in the next push (not yet pushed when written): the lookup now uses `system|version` when the expansion has a version and ignores a code system of any other version. `StatusComesFromTheCodeSystemVersionInTheExpansion` covers it (it fails without the fix).

We have introduced the class TerminologyServiceOperationExceptionExtensions class that codifies these errors based on the cause. Please read throiugh this class to understand its design (it has named functions that produce the correct issues), and use these instead. If you need to add a new function to that class, that's fine.
This will also make sure the errors are aligned with the (non public) terminology service operations in Vonk.

Thanks, done in d14a13e (not yet pushed when written). The tx-issue-type codes are private again. `TerminologyServiceOperationExceptionExtensions` now has an `extension(ValidateCodeResult)` block with cause-named methods that mirror the exception factories: `AddIncompleteCodedParameter`, `AddCodeNotInSystem`, `AddInvalidDisplay`, `AddUnprocessableCodedParameter` and `AddUnresolvable`. There are two new ones for causes the exceptions don't cover: `AddCodeNotInValueSet` (`not-in-vs`) and `AddCodeComment` (`code-comment`, a warning for inactive or deprecated concepts). `LocalTerminologyService` only uses these, and the generic `ValidateCodeResult.AddIssue` is now internal.

One difference from the exception factories: `AddInvalidDisplay` produces a warning with issue type `invalid` rather than an error with `code-invalid`. A wrong display doesn't make the code invalid here, and `invalid` is what the terminology ecosystem tests expect. Happy to align it with `InvalidDisplay` if you prefer.
